grades.quote: Eviction is expensive, so paging performs best if it’s infrequent: if applications use only a subset of their memory pages and the union of the subsets fits in RAM.
grades.reason: It explains why heavy paging is costly. Evicting pages is expensive, so paging only works well when it is infrequent and programs have good locality. When free memory is scarce, allocation requires eviction. This covers the mechanism behind constant paging with little useful work, but it never names thrashing or says outright that the system stops making progress.
